method.label: Split the solid into familiar pieces

annotationRationale: The key step identifies a composite solid consisting of a cylinder and two hemispheres. Cylinder and sphere volume formulas then determine the segment’s length.
sourceMethod: Follows the official cylinder-plus-two-hemispheres decomposition and volume equation, explaining the pieces using nearest points on the segment.

review.mathCheck: Points whose perpendicular projection lies on the segment form a radius-3 cylinder of height \(h=AB\); points beyond its endpoint planes form two hemispheres. These pieces meet only on boundary disks. Thus \(9\pi h+36\pi=216\pi\), giving \(AB=20\), choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of official solution 11 on attached page 4. It uses the same cylinder-and-hemispheres decomposition and volume equation, with a valid nearest-point explanation that accounts for both endpoints.
review.annotationCheck: Composite-solid recognition is appropriately assessed. Cylinder and sphere volume formulas are supporting knowledge, and all immediate nodes are used. The explanation is reconstructible with AMC 10 mathematics.
